From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Capacity check: late-stage deal — NebulaWorks sizing & provisional hold

Mike — good to chat earlier. NebulaWorks is moving to contract and procurement wants confirmation we can guarantee dedicated capacity for their production launch window (target: Aug 1 start, initial 6-month committed pool). High-level ask: a provisional hold on dedicated GPUs while legal and procurement close (they need a 30–45 day hold).

Quick context (attached pdf): they expect to run an ensemble of two open models (decoder-only 32B and a retriever-augmented ranking flow) with expected sustained inference of ~60 QPS peak across 8+ concurrent sessions, typical sequence length ~1024 tokens, and burst windows up to 150 QPS during batch jobs. They plan heavy embedding usage as well, parallel to inference flows.

Ben / Neha — can you run an internal availability check and advise: 1) what class of GPUs we'd map (A100-80GB equiv or H100?), 2) estimated node count and fractional capacity, 3) whether we can provision a soft hold (no billing) that auto-expires if contract doesn't sign within 45 days, and 4) rough monthly committed cost for customer-approved sizing to include in the SOW?

Attachments: nebula_requirements_v1.pdf (customer requirements summary)

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake

Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — looping infra early. Mike, quick clarifying Qs to keep the sizing tight:
- Target p99 latency SLO for user-facing requests? (<= 250ms token-generation or looser?)
- Are you flexible on quantization (8-bit or 4-bit acceptable) for the decoder model?
- Do you anticipate sustained long-running sessions (chat-like KV cache retention) versus largely stateless single-shot inference?

These change node count materially. If you prefer, we can treat this as two buckets: production steady-state (baseline) + scheduled batch windows (burst).

Neha — can you share a snapshot of capacity for us today (US region), plus policy for provisional holds (how many days, cancellation rights, whether holds are reversible without churn)? Also include an ETA for a soft hold ticket.

– Ben

Subject: Re: Capacity check: late-stage deal — NebulaWorks sizing & provisional hold

Jordan / Ben / Mike — reproduced inventory & ops analysis below. I pulled today’s US availability and ran a conservative mapping for NebulaWorks' profile.

Summary (short):
- Recommended mapping: H100-80GB class for the decoder-heavy 32B model (preferred for latency headroom), A100-80GB equiv can be offered with a quantified latency degradation.
- Baseline steady-state: estimate 6 H100 nodes (24 GPUs) to meet 60 sustained QPS with p99 token-generation <= 250ms using batching + KV cache affinity.
- Burst windows: allow a 2x burst factor for scheduled jobs (150 QPS) — reserve additional 12 GPUs in the pool (provisioned as hot-standby).
- Total suggested hold: 36 GPUs (can be a mix: 24 H100 + 12 A100 hot-standby) for initial commit.

Inventory snapshot (attached): inventory_snapshot_20270503.csv (current free GPUs in US pools):
- H100-80GB: 48 free
- A100-80GB equiv: 90 free
- NVLink-local nodes available: 18

Soft hold policy we can enact:
- We can place a provisional (soft) hold for up to 45 days without billing; hold requires 2-signature approval (Sales + Capacity Ops lead).
- Hold consumes logical capacity and will reduce free pool visibility to other deals; if not converted by day 45, hold auto-releases unless extended by mutual written agreement.
- Cancellation: customer can opt out early; we will not invoice for soft hold time but may require a short-notice operational fee if release is <7 days before other scheduled reassignments.

Estimated committed cost (monthly) for suggested pool (mix above, 6-month SOW ballpark):
- H100 unit monthly: $25,000 (list, datacenter-inclusive)
- A100 unit monthly: $14,000
- Estimated monthly committed spend (24 H100 + 12 A100 friction): $24x25k + 12x14k = $600k + $168k = $768,000/month (pre-negotiation; can trade-off with more quantization).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Sales: confirm the exact model mapping NebulaWorks prefers (H100-only vs mix).
2) Jordan: capture procurement's target hold window (they asked 30–45d).
3) Capacity Ops: I’ll submit a soft-hold ticket for 36 GPUs once Sales sign off and Legal gives provisional approval.

Attachments: inventory_snapshot_20270503.csv, provisional_hold_terms_v1.docx

Thanks team — that is very helpful. Confirmations:
- p99 latency target: <= 300ms token-generation for customer-facing endpoints (they can accept up to 300ms; shorter is a win).
- Quantization: engineering prefers 8-bit if it preserves accuracy; 4-bit acceptable only after a short eval (separate).
- Sessions: mix of long-running session affinity (KV cache) plus stateless batch ranking; KV retention is important.

We are comfortable with the recommended profile and would like Redwood to place the 36-GPU soft hold (24 H100 + 12 A100) while our legal team finalizes the contract. Procurement has requested the provisional_hold_terms_v1.docx and a short statement that holds are non-billing for the 45-day window. Sonia from procurement (cc'd) will own the paperwork side.

Please proceed to open the soft-hold ticket and send any internal approval artifacts you need from us. We’ll review the provisional terms and return comments within 48 business hours.
